To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phenylglyoxylated and 2,3-butane diomediated inactivation of Escherichia penicillin acylese are prevented by the substrates benzylpenicilline and phenylacetat.
penicillin acylation of penicillinase is a reversible reaction and the rate of penicillin hydrolysis is dependent on the nature of the acylating agent and on the nature of penicillin substrate.
phenylglyoxylated penicillin acrylate is inactive and that the phenylglyoxylation is reversible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanism and the structure-function relationship of the enzyme penicillin acyase.
the development of a novel method for the production of L-arginine.
the study of the mechanism and regulation of the biosynthesis of the penicillin antibiotics, and with the development of novel biocatalysts for the production of these antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the arginyl residue of penicillinase from Eschericia coli is involved in the catalytic process.
phenylglyoxalone inactivates penicillin acylation through modification of the arginine residue at or near the active site.
the arginyl residue is involved in catalysis of the penicillin acylation and that the reaction proceeds via a covalently linked enzyme-substrate intermediate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
penicillin acylation is the first reaction step in the catalytic mechanism of penicillin G acylase.
phenylglyoxals are useful reagents for the study of the active site of penicillins.

the catalytic site for penicillin acylation is a hydrophobic pocket, lined by a cluster of aromatic amino acids, and that a single essential arginyl residue, which may be involved in the binding of the carboxylate group of penicillins, is located at or near the entrance to the pocket.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phenylglyoxyl and 2,3-butandione are effective reagents for the identification of essential arginine residues in proteins.
phenylacetate and benzylpenicillins protect penicillin acylation and deacylation, but not deacylation of phenylacetate.
phenylglyoxals can be used as a probe to identify arginyl residues in proteins.
